text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Majali says King Hussein in good health and recuperating; king receives get-well wishes from Arab leaders.
- Appointment of 10 new judges in Justice Ministry, among them second woman judge in Jordan's judicial history.
- Higher Jordanian-Egyptian committee meets next month in Cairo to discuss bilateral ties.

- Mother of Jordanian soldier Ahmed Daqamsa who shot Israeli schoolgirls says she would have reacted more violently if she had been in her son's place; says family does not want money but wants her son to come back to her.
- Lawyer says did not see any signs of torture on Daqamsa.
- Islamists and centrists exchange verbal insults, centrist deputy Rawabdeh says Islamists exploiting sectarianism and racism to reach parliament.
- Supply Ministry reducing prices of fresh meat by 100 fils (14 U.S. cents) a kg; prices of vegetables drop.
- Saudi prince in charge of pilgrimage praises Jordanian-Saudi ties.
- Jordan ready to continue constructive efforts but rejects Israeli settlement policy.
